segments.text: Shiva was born from another god's anger. His first demand was not for power, it was for a name. Brahma, the creator, had made four sons from his mind. They were child sages called the Kumaras. He told them to help him fill the world with living beings. They folded their hands and said no. They said they were grateful, but they did not want to be bound by life and death. They wanted to meditate on the infinite. They asked only that they never grow old. Brahma argued, then gave in. As his sons left, rage rose in him. A fiery being burst from his forehead. A being stepped out of it with blazing red eyes. He roared, "What is my name?" Brahma sat in awe. The being roared again, "Tell me my name." Brahma remembered that the root word for both red and roaring is rud. He said, "Rudra, I name you Rudra." This was Shiva, also called Mahadev. Brahma created, Vishnu preserved, and Shiva was the destroyer. Brahma asked him to help with creation. Shiva agreed and began making beings, but he made copies of himself, and each was immortal. Eleven Rudras stood before Brahma. Brahma said creation needed mortals who die and are born again. Shiva said he could only make immortals. If that spoiled the plan, he would rather meditate. Then he left. The god born from Brahma's anger could only make what never dies.
